data.passageTitle: The Invention of the Television Part Two
data.passage:
As a student, Farnsworth began to try to come up with a way to catch pictures that move, change them to code, then move them to another device. His method used electrons to transmit the pictures. Farnsworth was not the first person to think about doing this, but he was the first person to make it work. There was instant recognition that, with this new invention, he was on to something big. In fact, by the 1930s, all televisions had been switched to the electronic method.

Before anyone knew it, the world’s first national television stations began to pop up. Then, more and more advancements with this fun device followed.

The first remote control that could change a channel or shut the TV off came along in 1955. During this same time, color TVs were on the rise. Today, we take this for granted. When is the last time you watched a black and white TV?

Now we have many options when looking to own a television. You can get one in any shape or size that you desire. We also find ourselves face to face with the temptation of online television and other innovations. Will these newest evolutions result in the extinction of the television as we know it? Only time will tell!
data.historyNote: Current records do not establish the next unread 7.4 passage. This passage follows the source sequence provisionally; repeat the last unread passage instead if classroom history shows otherwise.
